page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-24 is a network-optimized instance configuration built on the x86_64 processor architecture. It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 186.0 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation ratio of 7.75 GB of memory per core. The server configuration does not include any integrated GPUs, and no local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring storage to be provisioned separately through network-attached volumes.

The compute profile utilizes dedicated CPU allocation, avoiding multi-tenant core contention to deliver consistent computational execution. With no attached local disks, persistent storage lifecycle management is decoupled from the compute instance, allowing disk volumes to scale independently based on capacity and IOPS requirements. From a resource-density perspective, the high memory-to-core allocation provides substantial memory density without requiring excessive vCPU over-provisioning.

Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-24 is suited for workloads prioritizing substantial memory capacity alongside moderate multithreaded compute requirements. Target operational use cases include in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, memory-bound extraction and transformation pipelines, and enterprise application deployments requiring high memory headroom.
